items.title: White House Request Raises US AI Safety Center Independence Concerns
items.summary: The Associated Press reported on November 8, 2026, that officials at the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence, or CAISSI, had recently been asked to report informally to a White House office, raising concerns about the independence of federal AI safety evaluations.

items.title: Staff at the US center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — With public anxiety growing over mounting reports about out-of-control artificial intelligence agents, the tiny U.S. government division charged with assessing the safety of new AI offerings lacks a permanent leader and has stopped publishing its research.

items.title: AI safety advocates make gains after $110 million midterm fight
items.summary: Candidates who favor stricter oversight of artificial intelligence racked up wins in key congressional races, aided by a pro-regulation political funding group backed in part by Anthropic at a time when Americans are increasingly uneasy over the rapidly developing technology.
